context: Hiroshi briefs Kenji on a new corporate initiative.
purpose: boss-subordinate strategy briefing with N3 vocabulary

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 健次、新しい計画、簡単に、説明する。
lines.en: Kenji, I need you to brief me on the new plan. Keep it concise.
lines.style: Clipped, measured opening. No wasted breath. Authority sits naturally in the cadence. Lean forward slightly—attention focused, expecting the same back. Calm certainty underneath.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい、伺います。お願いします。
lines.en: Yes, sir. I'm ready to listen.
lines.style: Respectful attention. Slight nod in the voice. No hesitation, no over-explanation. Warm but professional—the kind of readiness that says he's genuinely prepared to take this in.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 海外の情報、増えてる。対応、急ぐ必要ある。
lines.en: We're getting more intelligence from overseas. We need to move fast on this.
lines.style: Weight on 'more' and 'fast.' Not alarmist, but the urgency is clear. Steady voice, no fluster. The kind of warning that comes from experience, not panic.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 理解しました。チーム、すぐ、集めます。
lines.en: Understood. I'll gather the team right away.
lines.style: Quiet snap to it. No dramatics. Just immediate commitment in the tempo—the voice quickens slightly, ready to move. Respectful but energized.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 重要な点、報告書、まとめろ。
lines.en: Pull the key points together and get me a full report.
lines.style: Direct instruction, not negotiable. But there's a lightness underneath—this is routine competence, not crisis management. Expects it will be done well.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 今週中に、提出いたします。
lines.en: I'll have it to you by end of week.
lines.style: Promise made simply. No over-assurance. The voice settles into reliability—measured, assured. This is a pledge he means to keep.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 頼むぞ。お前の判断、信頼している。
lines.en: I'm counting on you. I trust your judgment on this.
lines.style: Slight softening from the previous directness. Direct eye contact level in the voice. The compliment is genuine but not effusive—respect stated plainly, as fact.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: ありがとうございます。全力で、対応いたします。
lines.en: Thank you, sir. I won't let you down.
lines.style: Gratitude genuine and understated. Slight warmth enters the voice. Resolute closing—not a promise made lightly, but one he fully intends to keep. Dignity intact.
